{{short description|Mathematical conjecture}}

In [[rational homotopy theory]], the '''Halperin conjecture''' concerns the [[Serre spectral sequence]] of certain fibrations. It is named after the [[Canadian]] mathematician [[Stephen Halperin]].

== Statement ==
Suppose that <math> F \to E \to B </math> is a fibration of [[simply connected space]]s such that <math> F </math> is [[Rational homotopy theory#Elliptic and hyperbolic spaces|rationally elliptic]] and <math> \chi(F) \neq 0 </math> (i.e., <math> F </math> has non-zero [[Euler characteristic]]), then the [[Serre spectral sequence]] associated to the fibration collapses at the <math> E_2 </math> page.<ref>{{citation | last=Berglund | first=Alexander | title=Rational homotopy theory| year=2012 | url =  http://staff.math.su.se/alexb/rathom2.pdf}}</ref>

== Status ==
As of 2019, Halperin's conjecture is still open. Gregory Lupton has reformulated the conjecture in terms of formality relations.<ref>{{citation | last=Lupton | first=Gregory | title=Variations on a conjecture of Halperin | journal= Homotopy and Geometry (Warsaw, 1997)| year=1997 | arxiv=math/0010124 | mr=1679854 }}</ref>
